record.question:
A global mobile marketplace runs regional APIs and needs low-latency access to order-event metadata. Each event has a globally unique ID and is written in one Region. Users in other Regions may see a short replication delay. Payment settlement uses a separate authoritative system; this metadata store does not require cross-Region atomic transactions. The team wants local reads and writes without operating a custom replication service.

Which design best meets these requirements?

options.text: Create independent DynamoDB tables in each Region and use custom Lambda consumers to copy writes, handle retries, and prevent replication loops.
Create a DynamoDB global table with multi-Region eventual consistency and replicas in the required supported Regions. Have each API read and write its local replica.
Use CloudFormation StackSets to create identical DynamoDB tables in each Region and rely on StackSets to synchronize the data written to those tables.
Write metadata as objects to S3 buckets and configure cross-Region replication. Replace key-based database operations with object listings and custom metadata indexes.

explanation.text:
Correct: <<2>>. DynamoDB global tables provide managed multi-active replication, allowing the regional APIs to use local replicas. The stated tolerance for replication delay and single-Region ownership of each event fit multi-Region eventual consistency (MREC).

<<1>> can be built, but adds the replication, failure-handling, and loop-prevention code the team wants to avoid.

<<3>> synchronizes infrastructure deployment, not application records written into the tables.

<<4>> replicates objects but adds custom indexing to reproduce the stated database access pattern.

Do not infer cross-Region transactional guarantees from multi-Region replication. MREC can expose writes at different times in different Regions and requires conflict-aware design when multiple Regions modify the same item. DynamoDB also offers multi-Region strong consistency with its own supported configurations; choose the mode from the actual consistency requirements.

Official AWS references (checked 2026-09-18):
[DynamoDB global tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GlobalTables.html)
[Global-table replication and transactions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/globaltables-CoreConcepts.html)

diagram_alt: MREC local acknowledgement precedes guaranteed visibility in another Region; the application permits this delay.

MREC replication delay and transactional atomicity limited to the source Region
